01

Segmented engine

One file.
32 lanes.

Every download is split into segments fetched in parallel, then reassembled byte for byte. The live progress window shows each connection’s start position and progress.

  • Up to 32 connections per file, with a default maximum you can change in Options.
  • Per-connection map — see every segment’s position and the bytes it has received, live.
  • Integrity check confirms the pieces tile the whole file before it’s finished.
  • Single-connection fallback when a server has no Range support.
02

Dynamic segmentation

The slowest piece
gets help.

When a connection finishes, it doesn’t sit idle. It splits the slowest remaining piece in half and takes the second half, so one slow lane never drags out the finish.

  • Idle connections split the slowest segment in half, automatically.
  • Dead-connection detection: 30 seconds without data triggers a reconnect.
  • Adaptive connections: if a server answers extra connections with 429, 403 or 503, you get fewer, remembered per host for 24 hours.
  • Instant pause and shared rate pacing for speed limits.
Live simulation of the idea

8 lanes working…

03

Safe resume

Stop. Close.
Pick up.

Downloads survive restarts. State is saved in downloads.json, and DownCraft verifies the file before it continues.

  • ETag and size re-checked on resume. A file that changed on the server restarts instead of being corrupted.
  • Automatic retry with back-off after network errors, and a disk-space check before you start.
  • Duplicate links can show a dialog, so the same file is never fetched twice by accident.
  • HLS streams (.m3u8) are resumable too: best quality picked, AES-128 decrypted, saved as one file.

Options → Downloads: dialogs, duplicates, identification, resuming

04

Total control

Every knob.
Tabbed.

A full Options window with nine pages. Scroll to spin the stack: connections, proxy and site logins are all in there.

  • Connections: default maximum, exceptions for specific servers, per-download and global speed limits, retries.
  • Proxy / Socks: HTTP, SOCKS5 or system proxy, with credentials and a bypass list.
  • Site logins: HTTP Basic credentials, applied to the matching site or path only.
  • Network and extras: IPv4/IPv6 choice, timeouts, download quota, a command to run after each download, event sounds.

06

Browser extension

Hover.
Click. Saved.

A Manifest V3 extension for Chrome, Edge, Brave and Opera takes over browser downloads and puts a button on every video.

  • Download this video button in the corner of any video, plus a right-click “Download with DownCraft”. Alt+click bypasses it.
  • Direct links and HLS streams are listed in the toolbar popup, sent with referer and cookies.
  • YouTube via yt-dlp: formats grouped as Video + audio, Video only and Audio only, with codec and size.
  • Private by design: loopback-only at 127.0.0.1:19870, and nothing downloads until you confirm.
yt-dlp
ffmpeg
Deno

Install all three from Tasks → Tools

07

Queues & scheduler

Set it.
Walk away.

The IDM-style toolbar gives you everything in one row. Run the main queue, schedule it, and let DownCraft handle what happens when it’s done.

  • Start / Stop queue and a Scheduler for unattended runs.
  • When the queue ends: do nothing, close, sleep or shut down, with a 60-second cancel countdown.
  • Clipboard monitor offers to download links you copy, filtered by file type.
  • Auto categories: Compressed, Documents, Music, Programs, Video, each with its own folder.

And more

Small things,
done right.

Portable mode

Create a downcraft-data folder next to the executable and everything stays with it.

Toolbar skins

Load an IDM-style skin pack (.zip) from Options. Reset restores the built-in icons.

Batch add

Paste several URLs at once, one per line, in the Add download dialog.

Smart file names

Taken from Content-Disposition or the URL, then sorted into a category automatically.

Post-download command

Run a command after each download, for example a virus scan.

Start at login

Optional autostart, optionally minimised, and a system tray where the platform supports it.

Event sounds

Choose which events play a sound, from the Sounds page.

Download quota

Cap how much you download, set from the Connection page.
